transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Mark Liu (Evergreen Head of ML), Aisha Khan (Evergreen Platform Eng), Tom Reynolds (Evergreen CISO)

Summary (auto): Quick discovery on Dedicated capacity needs - reserved GPUs, isolation requirements, burst strategy, scaling expectations and security. Agreed to run benchmarks and share pricing + SOC2 docs.

Topics: Dedicated capacity overview, autoscaling & burst, network/isolation options (VPC), encryption/KMS, SSO/SAML, latency vs cost tradeoffs, pilot timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we got about 45 minutes, quick intros?
[00:10] Mark: Hi Mark Liu here, head of ML at Evergreen. We run inference for their advisor product and some back-office automation, thanks for setting up.
[00:18] Aisha: Aisha here, platform eng, I'll own infra side and networking.
[00:22] Tom: Tom, CISO, I'll listen for compliance and data residency questions.
[00:27] Samir: Perfect, I'm Samir AE at Redwood, and Lena our SE will cover technical details and benchmark plan.
[00:33] Lena: hi all, quick wave. we'll dig into Dedicated details and sizing.
[00:40] Samir: Mark, can you start with current stack and why you're looking at Dedicated vs hosted?
[00:48] Mark: Sure, currently we use a mix, some in-house models on k8s + a couple of managed endpoints on cloud. We're seeing spiky QPS during market hours and want predictable latency for our customer-facing assistant. Hosting on public Redwood hosted API is attractive, but we need guaranteed isolation and contractual SLAs - that's why Dedicated came up. Also some regulatory-ish constraints around PII in logs and retention.
[01:12] Lena: Makes sense. When you say spiky QPS can you ballpark numbers and token sizes?
[01:20] Mark: Right now peak is about 180 requests per second for the assistant, average tokens per request around 250, but we have longer sessions that push 1,200 tokens occasionally. Our p95 latency goal is under 300ms for short prompts, p99 under 800ms.
[01:40] Aisha: Also want isolation - can't have multi-tenant noisy neighbor; our infra team wants dedicated GPUs in our region with VPC peering and customer-managed KMS.
[01:52] Lena: All doable. Redwood Dedicated offers reserved GPU pools with VPC options and KMS/HSM integrations. For the burst pattern we usually see customers combine reserved base capacity plus burst-to-shared or burst-to-burst-only reserved for predictable headroom.
[02:10] Tom: Quick question on data residency and audit logs - do you keep inference logs in Redwood control plane? We need audit trails and an ability to disable persisting prompts.
[02:22] Samir: We have controls - you can disable retention and we can provide audit log exports. For Private deployments we can push control plane into your VPC, but Dedicated still gives you strong isolation - network-level peering, encryption at rest and in transit, and KMS for key control.
[02:38] Tom: Ok could you send SOC2 and network diagrams?
[02:42] Samir: Yup, will include that in follow-up.
[02:45] Mark: On the cost side, curious about cost per token for reserved versus hosted and how batching might reduce spend.
[02:53] Lena: Great question. With Dedicated we price the reserved GPU capacity (monthly commit) plus a usage overlay for burst. The unit cost is typically lower because you're amortizing the GPU across your workload. Also Redwood Optimize can recommend batching, KV cache (sometimes transcribed as KV cash in notes), and quantization profiles to drop unit cost. For latency-sensitive workloads we usually tune batching thresholds so short prompts don't wait.
[03:20] Mark: For our p95 target I can't tolerate batching that introduces +50ms.
[03:25] Lena: Understood. We can set dynamic batching with latency knobs. The runtime supports continuous batching and per-route SLOs so short routes skip batch queues or have smaller batch windows.
[03:34] Aisha: Talk to me about scaling. If we reserve, say, 4 A100-equivalent GPUs for baseline, how do we handle a sudden 3x spike?
[03:44] Lena: Two options: configure burst capacity within Dedicated (reserved burst pools you pay for as part of your contract) or fallback to hosted pool (we call it shared capacity) for overflow. For overflow to hosted, you have to accept cross-tenant execution, but it's isolated at the tenant level - still encrypted. Some customers prefer on-prem bursting or increasing reserved during known events.
[04:06] Mark: Is bursting to shared a hard no for security? For us, likely we need all inference to run on our reserved instances due to compliance.
[04:14] Tom: Yeah from CISO side we prefer no cross-tenant bursting; we might accept bursting to a separate dedicated burst pool that Redwood can allocate just for us temporarily.
[04:24] Samir: That's reasonable - we offer dedicated burst pools as an add-on so you don't fall back to public sharing. We'll note that as a requirement.
[04:31] Lena: For the benchmark we'll plan to use reserved-only and dedicated burst so results reflect that isolation.
[04:36] Mark: Good. Now about model choices - we have some Llama-variant and a couple of proprietary fine-tuned models. Any constraints on model size or kv cache behavior?
[04:48] Lena: Runtime supports large models and handles KV cache management. For very long sessions we can pin longer KV caches but that increases memory. Also we do quantization-aware kernels; performance/latency depends on model arch and sequence length. We'll recommend model variants and quantization that hit your latency SLOs.
[05:06] Mark: Are we able to bring our own model artifacts? We can't send weights out of our network ideally.
[05:13] Samir: For Private deployments you can keep everything on-prem or in your VPC. For Dedicated we typically pull the model into the dedicated GPU pool in our region - but we have NDA and secure transfer options. If you can't move weights, Private is the route.
[05:27] Aisha: For networking, do you support private peering, ingress VPC endpoints, and egress controls?
[05:33] Lena: Yes - VPC peering, private endpoints, and strict egress rules are supported. We can also restrict control plane API to your IP ranges.
[05:41] Tom: KMS integration - can we use our AWS KMS or an HSM?
[05:45] Samir: Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported; HSM integrations available for Private. We'll include a short KMS integration note in the docs.
[05:54] Mark: For observability, we need token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency and traces.
[05:59] Lena: Redwood Console provides per-route dashboards, token-level cost, and tracing hooks you can forward to your APM. We can provision RBAC so only certain roles see cost data.
[06:11] Aisha: On the ops side, who handles OS/driver updates for the GPUs and how are maintenance windows scheduled?
[06:18] Lena: For Dedicated we manage the runtime and patching, but maintenance windows are scheduled with you and we provide 72-hour notice for non-emergency maintenance. You can opt into fixed update windows.
[06:29] Mark: In terms of SLA, what's the typical availability guarantee for Dedicated?
[06:33] Samir: We offer SLA-backed uptime for Dedicated - typical is 99.9% with credits for downtime. Exact terms depend on contract tier.
[06:42] Tom: Do you have penetration testing reports or a vulnerability disclosure program?
[06:46] Samir: Yes, we have a VDP and we can share recent pen test summaries.
[06:50] Mark: How long is onboarding and what's the pilot look like?
[06:54] Lena: Pilot is usually 2-4 weeks: sizing + benchmark, pass/fail on latency/cost, then a short stabilization. For Dedicated we spin a reserved pool in your preferred region (2-5 business days depending on capacity).
[07:07] Mark: We have a quarterly spike around options expiration mid-April - would like to have Dedicated for that event. Is that timeline feasible?
[07:14] Samir: If we start the pilot this month and finish benchmarks by mid-March, we can secure capacity and have prod-ready by early April. We'll need to lock commitments sooner to reserve GPU inventory.
[07:25] Aisha: Any specific telemetry you need from our side for benchmarking?
[07:29] Lena: We'll ask for request histograms (qps distribution by minute), average/95/99 token counts, common prompt templates, and examples of long-running sessions. Also any special I/O like attachments.
[07:41] Mark: We'll export that and send it over.
[07:44] Tom: If we go Dedicated, can logs be routed to our SIEM and masked before leaving the VPC?
[07:51] Samir: Yes, log forwarding to your SIEM is standard; we can also support on-prem log collectors in Private mode. Alerting and masking rules can be implemented on ingest.
[08:01] Lena: Quick note on model rollouts - Dedicated supports canary + A/B with automatic fallback to previous model versions to avoid regressions.
[08:10] Mark: That's important, we saw regressions in a previous rollout.
[08:14] Samir: Ok quick recap - actions: send pricing and SOC2 + pen test summary; Lena to draft benchmark plan; Mark to send traffic profiles; schedule deep technical session week of Mar 16. Any other asks?
[08:28] Tom: Please add dedicated burst pools (no shared bursting) as a firm requirement in the SOW.
[08:34] Samir: Noted.
[08:36] Mark: Also include estimated lead time to provision extra capacity if we decide to scale mid-quarter.
[08:41] Samir: Will include.
[08:44] Aisha: Thanks team - we'll review docs and sync after you send the plan.
[08:48] Samir: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the deck and next steps.

End of transcript.
